title: Sames Scholars Program marks 24 years of scholarships and mentoring for Laredo students
excerpt: The Sames Scholars Program marked 24 years of helping Laredo students reach college with a kickoff orientation Tuesday at Texas A&M International University, where organizers said the program has awarded more than $2 million in scholarships and seen nearly 100 students graduate.
content:
The Sames Scholars Program marked 24 years of helping local students reach college with a kickoff orientation on Tuesday at the Texas A&M International University Student Center Ballroom in Laredo, according to KGNS.

The program supports first-generation and other college-bound students with scholarships and mentoring, pairing United Independent School District high school students with TAMIU faculty mentors who guide them through high school and into college.

Co-founder Elizabeth Sames, who started the program with her husband Hank in 2002, said education is something no one can take away. “Education is the one thing that no one can take from you,” Sames said, according to KGNS.

To stay in the program, students must be first-generation college-bound, meet economically disadvantaged state criteria, maintain a 90 percent grade-point average and 95 percent attendance, and meet monthly with their TAMIU mentor, according to TAMIU.

Since its founding, the program has awarded more than $2 million in scholarships and nearly 100 students have graduated, according to KGNS.

The kickoff orientation welcomed the program’s newest cohort of high school students, continuing a model that has paired Laredo teenagers with university mentors for more than two decades.

Sources: KGNS, November 10, 2026; Texas A&M International University.
